test: vector-search freshness at RF=3 under vector-search=LOCAL_ONE

target.product: HCD 2.0.6 (5.0.7.0-ea50e91ba01f), Data API v1.0.33 temporary container
target.vector_collection: dim 16, cosine; Data API defaults writes/reads=LOCAL_QUORUM, vector-search=LOCAL_ONE, serial=LOCAL_SERIAL (M6)
target.validity_check: marker vector returns at cosine similarity 1.0 rank-1, background at <=0.83; an unrelated query returns a different top-1 — the ANN search discriminates, the hit is not trivial

verdict: NOT DETECTABLE on this topology (neither confirms nor refutes the article's section-4 [D] claim)
reasoning: 120/120 cycles (60 idle + 60 under 40 vector-writes/s): the just-written vector was top-1 on the FIRST LOCAL_ONE search in every cycle; 0 cycles where the LOCAL_QUORUM key read found the document but the LOCAL_ONE vector search missed it.

The insert->vector-visible interval is dominated by the two HTTP round trips (idle p50 74.7 ms, loaded p50 74.4 ms), not by replication: on this single-host ring inter-replica latency is sub-millisecond, so by the time the LOCAL_ONE search arrives the third replica already carries the write.
The LOCAL_ONE risk is therefore real in principle but bounded here BELOW the ~74 ms measurement floor. This bench cannot show it because it cannot make a replica lag longer than an HTTP round trip.
what_this_does_not_establish: That no window exists: a real multi-datacentre (WAN) deployment, where inter-replica latency is tens of milliseconds, is exactly where LOCAL_ONE could return a stale vector — and that is the topology the article's 'wide-area' framing targets. This single-host ring cannot reproduce it.

Separation of replication lag from JVector index-build lag: with 0 miss, the two cannot be disambiguated here. A second Data API at vector-search=LOCAL_QUORUM would only matter once a WAN topology makes misses appear.
Anything about vectorize/embedding-gateway paths (VECTORIZE_ENABLED=false here), other dimensions/metrics, or larger corpora.
article_bearing: Section 4 [D] 'searchable as soon as it is written' is quoted from HCD docs about JVector adding documents to the graph immediately. This test adds one qualifier the article does not: at RF>1 the Data API READS vector search at LOCAL_ONE while it WRITES at LOCAL_QUORUM, so 'searchable at acknowledgement' is a single-replica read guarantee, not a quorum one. On co-located replicas the gap is unobservable; on a WAN it is the exact shape of window the article warns about for the OTHER engine (MongoDB, figure 2). Worth a one-line [M]/[U] footnote, not a claim change.
